boxes.reason: D3D on vcr-kmd is supervised-only. Red Faction is Direct3D 8 only.
Windows 7 on the Standard VGA stub: no 3D driver for rf.exe's D3D8, and no disc mounter.
Operator override 'not wanted on .243' in gamegate overrides.txt; also below RF's floors (P166 against 300 MHz, 127 MB against 128 MB).

summary: 7 boxes (.110 .123 .133 .143 .171 .184 .240) were proven in ONE TeamDM game on .123's dedicated server. My own UDP query read 7/16, and the fresh scoreboard frames name all 7 Fleet<octet> players. .124 is BLOCKED (D3D on vcr-kmd is supervised-only). .186 and .243 are NA. The game was closed everywhere and no rf.exe remains. ForcePort on .123 was reset to 0 and read back.
issues: lanparty.py has no 'rf' roster kind, so its roster reads null and on_server '?'. The witness was a manual UDP query (00 00 00) to .123:7755 plus the in-game scoreboards.
In the RF query reply the 0x87 marker sits at byte 4, not byte 3 as recipes.json says.
No packet counts: the host is a fleet box, so tcpdump on .132 cannot see the client traffic.
kill had to force rf.exe on 6 of 7 boxes. WM_CLOSE did not end RF within 12 s; only .133 closed gracefully. No crash dialogs: every foreground afterwards is the agent or chat console.
The kill CLI takes the title as a positional argument; the documented 'kill --game RedFaction' fails with 'unrecognized arguments'.
gamestart.txt was left on the boxes; it is harmless.
library_fix_needed: The compat DB still says Red Faction LAN is needs_human. It is now proven automatable: ListLAN=1, then MULTI > JOIN GAME > the server row > Join at 640x480.
